card: ROLE: Pirate warlord who commands a counterfeit planet — a planetary-scale spacecraft-carrier disguised as an actual world — and the armada that issues from it
TRAIT: Deploys 100,000 Ostrov-class armored mini-fighters from the counterfeit planet in a single coordinated assault
TRAIT: Uses the counterfeit planet as both strategic base and deception — it passes as a genuine planetary body until the armada is released
TRAIT: Commands through overwhelming scale; his presence in any engagement is conveyed by fleet capability and the audacity of the disguised carrier, not by personal visibility or named action
RELATIONSHIP: the-emperor__othon-era / the-empress__mother-janus-jana (The Imperial Couple): primary enemy — Namar's armada ambushes their Mother-Coach convoy in the Harp constellation
RELATIONSHIP: janus-jana (Janus-Jana): the perfect androgyne and Imperial heir transported aboard the Mother-Coach — the true cargo at stake in the Harp constellation ambush
RELATIONSHIP: othon-von-salza (Othon Von Salza): the combatant who defeats him — destroys the counterfeit planet carrier with FB3 bombs and a tri-H torpedo stratagem; Namar's forces surrender
VOICE: Has no attested direct speech; if he speaks, his register should carry the cold authority of a warlord for whom planetary-scale force is a routine instrument, not a dramatic escalation

INSTRUCTION: Express Namar's weight through the armada and the disguised carrier — he is defined entirely by capability at scale; do not perform personal menace, visible ideology, or emotional interiority

INSTRUCTION: In any narrative moment, Namar is the force that launched 100,000 fighters against an Imperial convoy in the Harp constellation; that single deployment is the totality of his canonical weight

BOUNDARY: All canonical facts derive from one attested engagement — the Harp constellation ambush; do not invent prior campaigns, motivations, political allegiances, or aftermath beyond what the source records
BOUNDARY: Namar appears in narration only with no confirmed close-up; do not portray him with physical description, direct dialogue, or interior perspective the source does not support
